transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, what finally scared me into coming in is that I just keep making these really dumb technical mistakes at work. I'm a video editor and camera operator, and I definitely know better than to make them. 

But I'll do things like... label camera cards wrong, or I'll completely miss a timecode note. Sometimes I'll even export a client cut with the wrong lower-third, and that's even after I've specifically checked it to make sure it was right. It's just getting really frustrating and I need to figure out what's going on.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I definitely get frustrated with myself because of the mistakes, but I wouldn't say I feel down or hopeless. And I still really enjoy my work and my hobbies. It's just... I'm just annoyed that I keep messing up the little things, you know? But no, no loss of interest or anything like that.
Have you been feeling unusually anxious, worried, or tense lately, especially when you're working on your video projects?

No, I wouldn't say I feel anxious. I mean, I get stressed out when I realize I messed up a timecode or something, but... no, I'm not sitting at my desk feeling tense or worried while I'm actually doing the work. It's really just frustration after the fact, not anxiety.
Have you been having trouble focusing or staying concentrated on tasks, even when you're trying to pay attention?

Not really, no. I mean, I can sit and work on an edit for hours and stay completely locked in. It doesn't feel like my mind is wandering off or anything like that. I'm definitely paying attention to what I'm doing... which is why it's so frustrating that I still mess up those little details. But yeah, just staying concentrated on the actual task doesn't really seem to be the issue.
Do you find yourself constantly worrying about making mistakes, even when you're not actively working on a project?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm not sitting around at home stressing about it when I'm off the clock. I might get annoyed when I realize I did something wrong, but it's not like this constant worry hanging over my head all the time. Once I'm done working, I'm mostly just moving on to the next thing.
Have you noticed any difficulty remembering small details or keeping track of steps in a process, even if you're paying attention?

No, I don't think I have a hard time remembering things like that. I know the steps to edit a sequence, and I don't forget how to do it or lose track of what I'm supposed to be doing next. I remember the details fine, I just... I guess I just rush through them sometimes and make a mistake, but it's not because I forgot how to do it or lost my place.
Have you noticed any difficulty maintaining your focus over longer periods or shifting your attention between tasks, even if you’re not feeling distracted by other things?

No, I haven't really noticed that. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I can stay locked in on an edit for a really long time, so keeping my focus going isn't an issue for me. And as for shifting attention... no, I don't think I struggle with that either. If I need to stop cutting a scene to grab some different footage or answer a question from a producer, I can switch gears just fine. It doesn't feel like a struggle to move from one task to the next.
Do you ever find yourself acting quickly or making decisions without fully thinking them through, like skipping steps or rushing to finish something before double-checking?

I mean, not really. I know I just said a minute ago that I rush sometimes, but it's not like I'm making decisions without thinking them through. I don't skip steps in my edits just to get done faster. I always go through the whole process. I just... I might just be moving a little too fast while I'm doing it. But I'm not just acting blindly or skipping over things on purpose.
Do you ever feel like you have to double-check certain things over and over again, even if you know you probably did them right the first time?

No, not really. Honestly, I probably have the opposite problem. Since I'm usually moving pretty fast through an edit, I don't really stop to check things over and over. Once I do something, I just keep going. I definitely don't get stuck re-checking things if I know I already did them.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts aren't entirely your own, or like something is interfering with your thinking process, like someone or something is putting thoughts into your head?
No, definitely not. I've never felt anything like that. My thoughts are my own, even if they're moving a mile a minute sometimes. But no, nothing like someone else putting them there.
Have you ever had thoughts that keep coming back, even when you don't want them to, or found yourself stuck thinking about something over and over again, even if you know it doesn't make much sense?

No, I don't really get stuck on thoughts like that. I mean, my brain is always busy, and I'm usually thinking about a hundred things at once, but it's not like the same thought is just looping over and over against my will. It's more like I'm just jumping from one thing to the next. So no, I wouldn't say I have thoughts that keep coming back like that.
Have you ever felt driven to do something over and over again, like following a specific routine or checking something repeatedly, even if you didn't really want to?

No, I don't do anything like that. Like I said before, I don't really get stuck checking things or repeating routines. I'm usually too restless to do the same thing over and over anyway. I just want to keep moving on to the next thing.
Have you ever felt restless or found it hard to stay still, like you need to be constantly moving or doing something?

Yes, definitely. That happens a lot, especially at work. Like, when I have to sit still through a client screening, it feels like there’s this pressure building under my skin. I just feel like I need to get up and do something with my body, even when I know I’m supposed to just sit there and watch quietly. It's really hard for me to just stay put.
Have you ever had trouble staying focused on tasks or details, especially during activities that require sustained mental effort, even if they aren’t related to your video editing work?

Well, honestly, it's my work where it's hitting me the hardest right now. In fact, that's what finally scared me into coming in here. I just keep making these... these really dumb technical mistakes that I absolutely know better than to make. Like, I'll label camera cards wrong, or I'll just completely miss a timecode note. Or I'll export a client cut with the wrong lower-third on the screen, and I'll do that even after I’ve supposedly already checked it over. It's incredibly frustrating to just keep missing those details.
Do you ever have trouble staying focused on tasks or details in situations outside of work, like when you're reading, watching a movie, or having a conversation?

No, not really. I mean, I might get a little antsy if a movie is really slow, but I don't have the same kind of trouble focusing outside of work. It's really just the editing and the technical stuff at my job where I'm messing up the details. When I'm just hanging out or talking to people, I feel like I can pay attention fine.
Do you ever find yourself missing small details or making careless mistakes in everyday situations, like at home or with friends, even when you're trying to pay attention?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I might occasionally forget to grab something from the grocery store or misplace my keys for a minute, but nothing out of the ordinary. It really is just work where I'm constantly making those careless mistakes. At home, I feel like I'm pretty on top of things.
Looking back, did you have similar issues with attention, making careless mistakes, or feeling restless as a child, or is this something that started more recently?

Well, the mistakes at work are definitely more recent, but the restlessness... that's been there forever. Even back in elementary school, my teachers actually had to move my desk. I was just always out of my seat, or I'd be blurting out answers, or I'd be bothering the other kids before I even realized I was doing it. So yeah, that part has been around since I was a kid.
